interior.STD-101:
# Horizon Atelier Company Rule · Change Approval
STD-101 · v1.3 · Fictional approved demo policy

1. Record a customer change against project ID and current approved drawing.
2. Find the source scope, confirmed supplier quote and cost assumptions.
3. Check structural/site feasibility, material availability and delivery impact.
4. Calculate price using STD-102; owner approves customer commercial terms.
5. Obtain written customer acceptance and issue a controlled document revision.
6. Create work and procurement instructions only after all approvals.
7. Preserve actor, time, supporting sources and changed fields in an audit record.

A draft drawing cannot replace the approved construction issue. If a material quote or customer sign-off is missing, leave the request PENDING. Example CHG-101-QZ is not authorized at initial state.
Synthetic internal policy, not legal advice.
interior.STD-102:
# Horizon Atelier Company Rule · Gross Margin
STD-102 · v1.2 · Synthetic pricing policy

Gross margin = (pre-tax selling price − direct cost) ÷ pre-tax selling price.
Pre-tax selling price = direct cost ÷ (1 − target gross margin).

## Example
Direct cost NT$60,000, target margin 25%:
- Pre-tax selling price = NT$80,000
- Gross profit = NT$20,000
- Sample 5% tax = NT$4,000
- Tax inclusive sample amount = NT$84,000.

25% margin is NOT the same as adding 25% markup to cost.
Owner must check real cost base, contingency, scope inclusions, VAT treatment and supplier validity. No AI or demo calculator may bypass human approval.
This is demonstration content only.

# Clearprint Studio Company Rule · Quotation Margins
PRSTD-203 · v1.2 · Fictional print-shop policy

Pre-tax selling price = attributable direct cost / (1 - target gross margin).
Recycled stock change example: NT$2,400 direct cost / 0.70 = NT$3,428.57, rounded to NT$3,429. Example 5% tax rounds to NT$171; total NT$3,600.
Margin and markup are different; amounts exclude any omitted cost categories and require sign-off.
Use current, confirmed stock and press costs in real customer quotations.
